newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore office rents seen easing further.
newsitem.headline: Singapore office rents seen easing further.

text.p: Singapore office rents and capital values are likely to soften further this year with more new office space becoming available, real estate firm Edmund Tie & Company (ET&C) said on Thursday.

In its first quarter review of the Singapore property market, ET&C said average rents in the prime Raffles Place area eased by five percent to an average Singapore $10 per sq ft a month over the last quarter of 1996.
However, office occupancy remained relatively stable at 94 percent during the quarter.
"With the considerable supply of new offic space expected to come on stream, the office market is likely to consolidate with an overall softening of rentals and capital values," said ET&C.
The market expects a new supply of office space amounting to 4.1 million sq ft to be completed by the end of 1997.
ET&C said sentiment on the residential market picked up slightly during the first quarter.
"Market activity picked up particularly for new launches of condominiums and landed property," it said.
Developers launched 1,800 new housing units during the quarter compared with 3,100 units in the last quarter of 1996.
